interest:
I study JWST observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN, especially
little red dots (LRDs), compact red sources, dust-reddened or broad-line AGN,
early black-hole growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution at cosmic dawn.

Prioritize papers about:
1. JWST/NIRCam/NIRSpec/MIRI observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN
2. little red dots, compact red galaxies, obscured AGN, broad-line AGN, and
   high-redshift black hole candidates
3. SED fitting, spectroscopy, emission lines, photometric redshifts, stellar
   masses, dust attenuation, AGN contamination, and source classification
4. high-redshift galaxy formation, reionization-era galaxies, early SMBH
   growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution
5. survey papers from CEERS, JADES, UNCOVER, COSMOS-Web, PRIMER, GLASS,
   RUBIES, and similar JWST deep fields

Also keep papers about AI, machine learning, large language models (LLMs),
large multimodal models (LMMs), foundation models, anomaly detection,
automated classification, spectral/photometric inference, or research agents
when they are applied to astronomy, astrophysics, JWST data, galaxy surveys,
AGN selection, or literature/data analysis.

Deprioritize unrelated stellar, solar-system, local-universe, gravitational
wave, or purely theoretical papers unless they directly inform high-redshift
galaxies, AGN, JWST analysis, or AI-for-astronomy workflows.

papers.title: The Ĝ Infrared Search for Extraterrestrial Civilizations with Large Energy Supplies. V. When Galaxies Glow with Industry
papers.authors: Olivia Curtis , Aidan J. Rowland , Jason T. Wright , Caryl Gronwall , Jakob M. Helton , Joel Leja
papers.abstract: We present the most robust stellar population synthesis (SPS)-based search for galaxy-spanning technological waste heat to date, applied to 129 nearby galaxies spanning a wide range of spectral energy distribution (SED) types, including ultraluminous IR galaxies and MIR-luminous active galactic nuclei (AGN). We incorporate the AGENT Dyson sphere formalism into the Flexible Stellar Population Synthesis code at the stellar population level, so nebular and dust emission respond self-consistently to Dyson sphere reprocessing. With \texttt{Prospector}, we perform a suite of 1,419 injection recovery tests across a range of covering fractions, $\alpha$, where we successfully recover the injected covering fractions (best-fit slope $m = 0.92$) and detect them through Bayesian model selection down to $\alpha \sim 4$--$5\%$ in quiescent galaxies. None of our 129 galaxies prefer a Dyson sphere component, and we place the first per-galaxy 95\% upper limits on warm ($T_{\rm BB} \gtrsim 100$K) swarms, reaching a median $\alpha < 0.3\%$ across quiescent hosts without a dominant AGN. Our injection-calibrated detection rates convert these zero detections into a population bound of $<2.6\%$ of galaxies hosting $\alpha = 25\%$ swarms ($95\%$ confidence). Because survey colors cannot separate waste heat from starbursts and AGN, we develop a scaffold for future searches, running from inexpensive archival screens such as the Balmer decrement and the stellar-to-dynamical-mass offset a swarm leaves behind, through resolved fitting with nuclear excision, to PRIMA FIR photometry that makes targeted JWST imaging decisive. We find that the outskirts of quiescent galaxies are the best hunting grounds for future technosignature searches.
papers.Reasons for match: Focuses on Dyson spheres and technosignatures in nearby galaxies, not high-redshift JWST galaxies or AGN. The SED fitting methodology could be tangentially relevant but the science case is unrelated.
papers.Short digest: The central question is whether galaxy-spanning Dyson spheres can be detected in nearby galaxy SEDs. The main result is no detection of Dyson sphere components in 129 nearby galaxies, with upper limits on covering fractions. This is not directly relevant to high-redshift galaxy/AGN studies but the SED fitting framework might inform similar analyses.
Full-text inspection checklist: Check if the SED fitting framework could be adapted for high-redshift AGN/galaxy SEDs
Look for any discussion of AGN contamination in SED fitting that could be relevant

papers.title: Waterfall-modulated $α$-attractors
papers.authors: Renata Kallosh , Andrei Linde , Yusuke Yamada
papers.subjects: Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO) ; General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology (gr-qc); High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)
papers.abstract: Hybrid $\alpha$-attractor models \cite{Kallosh:2022ggf} can have significantly greater values of $n_{s}$ and smaller $r$, while preserving the relation $r\cong 3\alpha (1-n_s)^2$, which is valid for exponential T- and E-models at large values of the inflaton field. Here we study single-field $\alpha$-attractors with features inspired by hybrid models: one can uplift the potential, and one can also have a waterfall regime that leads to a premature termination of inflation near the critical point $\varphi_c$. This allows one to increase the effective number of e-foldings $N_c$ in formulas like $n_s\simeq 1-{2\over N_c}$, $r\simeq {12 \alpha\over N_c^2}$. By changing the waterfall's steepness and location, one can continuously move the predictions along the curves with $r\cong 3\alpha (1-n_s)^2$ as $n_s$ increases and $r$ decreases. We also study the effect of waterfall insertions and uplift on $n_s$ in quintessential $\alpha$-attractors that describe inflation and dynamical dark energy.
papers.Reasons for match: This paper is about inflationary cosmology and alpha-attractors, not related to high-redshift galaxies, AGN, or JWST observations.
papers.Short digest: The central question is how waterfall features in alpha-attractor models affect inflationary predictions. The main result is that such features can increase the effective number of e-foldings, shifting predictions along the r-ns relation. This is irrelevant to my work on JWST high-redshift galaxies and AGN.

papers.title: Differential Reddening and Extinction Law Analyses of Galactic Open Clusters
papers.authors: Xiaohan Chen , Shu Wang , Xiaodian Chen
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Solar and Stellar Astrophysics (astro-ph.SR)
papers.abstract: Extinction significantly affects open cluster parameters and their use in studies of Galactic structure, yet homogeneous large sample measurements of open cluster extinction properties remain limited. Using Gaia-era open cluster member samples combined with multi-band photometry and stellar parameters, we derive color excesses of member stars and provide the homogeneous characterization of the mean reddening, differential reddening, and color excess ratio (CER) at the cluster scale. Differential reddening increases systematically with mean reddening, with highly reddened clusters near the Galactic plane showing stronger extinction variations. Star-by-star reddening corrections narrow color--magnitude diagram (CMD) sequences in 369 of 435 clusters (85%) with reliable CMD-width measurements, and cluster color excess maps reveal small-scale extinction structures. The median CER is compatible with the standard diffuse interstellar medium extinction curve, while the broad CER distribution and its large-scale variations across the Galactic disk likely reflect differences in the dominant dust environments sampled along different Galactic sight lines.
papers.Reasons for match: Focuses on Galactic open clusters and extinction laws, not high-redshift galaxies or AGN.
papers.Short digest: The paper studies extinction properties of Galactic open clusters. It finds differential reddening increases with mean reddening and that star-by-star corrections improve CMDs. This is unrelated to JWST high-redshift studies.
Full-text inspection checklist: Check if any cluster extinction results could inform dust laws for high-z galaxies
Look for any mention of JWST or high-redshift applications
